newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds ease in line with overseas markets.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds ease in line with overseas markets.

text.p: Irish government bonds eased in thin trade on Thursday in line with most international markets, dealers said.

Dealers said German bunds had extended losses as the market remained convinced no more rate cuts were likely in the near term, while UK gilts fell across the curve despite a seemingly successful auction of 8.0 percent stock due 2015.

The 1.5 billion stg of stock was covered 2.66 times but UK dealers said the market weakened after the European Court upheld a move by Unilever and Argos to have the British government pay back excess VAT paid on discounted goods.
The UK Treasury said the maximum cost to the government from the ruling would be 200 million stg. But tax experts said the worst-case scenario could cost them 500 million stg.
Dealers said the story had been used as an excuse for the gilt-market to sell-off.
In the U.S., dealers said Treasuries were under pressure in late morning trade and could go lower.
By 1525 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2000 had eased 18p to 106.54 to yield 6.00 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had eased 20p to 107.50 to yield 6.80 percent.
